title: Docs deliverables: KMS rotation procedure, troubleshooting guide, and Security FAQ deltas
creator: Talia Benson
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation — KMS hardening + rotation
description:
Goal
Ship a complete, reviewed docs package for the KMS hardening + rotation work across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, with clear separation between public/customer-facing content and restricted/internal runbooks.

Scope / deliverables
1) Private deployment operator procedure (Day-2 ops)
- Source of truth: Confluence (restricted): sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/private-kms-rotation-procedure.json
- Public/Customer-facing: Redwood Docs (sanitized, no internal endpoints or toggles)
- Must cover:
  - Preconditions: supported KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault where applicable), region constraints, required IAM/KMS key policy statements, and installer preflight expectations
  - Rotation types: scheduled vs emergency (and how they differ operationally)
  - Step-by-step rotation workflow, including dual-read window behavior (what “rotation started” vs “rotation complete” means)
  - Validation checklist: smoke tests, decrypt/encrypt verification, audit log verification, how to confirm key-version pinning config is active
  - Rollback guidance (bounded) and when to stop vs continue
  - Common failure cases: AccessDenied, Disabled key/version, NotFound, throttling, timeouts, region/API outages; what to check first
  - Shared responsibility boundaries (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood control plane responsibilities)

2) Troubleshooting guide (Private-first, but usable by SRE/Support)
- Customer-facing troubleshooting doc (public): symptoms → likely causes → safe actions
- Internal runbook cross-links (restricted):
  - KMS dependency degradation runbook: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/kms-dependency-degradation-runbook.json
  - Alerting + dashboards references (no internal URLs in public version)
- Must include:
  - “KMS brownout” vs “hard outage” characterization
  - What information to capture for escalation: timestamps, provider, key ID alias (sanitized), error codes, circuit breaker state, cache hit rate changes
  - Guidance on how to interpret new observability signals (ENG-4239)

3) Security FAQ deltas + enterprise response snippets
- Update existing Security/Enterprise FAQ pages with:
  - Rotation cadence guidance (default recommendations; what customers can configure)
  - Emergency rotation definition, triggers, and expected downtime/behavior
  - Backwards compatibility guarantees for existing ciphertext and rollback semantics (aligned with ADR-0142)
  - Audit logging: what events are produced and retention expectations (high-level)
  - Evidence package pointers for GRC (what we can provide on request)
- Ensure language is consistent with: drive draft Q&A (customer-facing)
  - sources/google_drive/shared_drives/security-and-compliance/kms-rotation-customer-qna-draft.json

Review + publication workflow
- Content owners:
  - Elliot Price (overall editorial + docs repo PR)
  - Kira Thompson (operator/runbook structure + troubleshooting flow)
  - Marcus Lin (security review + wording on guarantees)
  - Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes (SRE review: degradation actions + safe toggles)
  - Olga Petrov / Daniel Carter (GRC alignment: control mapping + evidence phrasing)
- Publication targets:
  - Docs PR (redwood-docs): PR-1187 is the intended carrier for initial publication
  - Restricted Confluence pages updated in parallel; ensure public pages do not include internal-only flags, endpoints, or tenant identifiers

Acceptance criteria
- Rotation procedure is complete and matches implemented behavior (dual-read window, key-version pinning, installer preflights).
- Troubleshooting guide includes at least 6 concrete scenarios with actions and escalation criteria:
  1) AccessDenied / policy denial
  2) Disabled key / disabled key version
  3) Throttling (429/Throttled) sustained
  4) Timeouts / elevated latency
  5) Region or KMS API partial outage
  6) Misconfigured key alias / wrong key version pinned
- Security FAQ deltas reviewed by Security + GRC and approved for enterprise sharing.
- Docs are published with correct access boundaries (public vs restricted) and linked from relevant enterprise/security pages.
- Support is provided a short internal “copy/paste” snippet set for common customer questions (rotation cadence, ‘what is rotation complete’, audit evidence availability).

Open questions / risks
- Wording risk: avoid promising “no downtime” universally; must describe expected behavior under degraded KMS and dual-read window limitations.
- Provider differences: ensure AWS/GCP/Azure terminology is correct (key version vs key rotation semantics vary).
- Backwards compatibility: align with ADR-0142; ensure no doc implies plaintext re-encryption is required for all artifacts.

Links
- ADR: adr-0142-kms-rotation-contracts-and-backwards-compat (Confluence)
- Audit events spec: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/kms-key-lifecycle-audit-events.json
- Docs publication PR (target): sources/github/redwood-docs/pr_1187.json
- Installer preflight notes (edge cases): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/private-deployments/private-kms-install-preflight-notes.json
